'''Exar Kun''' was a [[Dark Lord of the Sith]] who flourished thousands of [[Standard year|years]] before [[Darth Sidious]] and his [[Sith apprentice]] [[Maul|Darth Maul]].<ref name="Altaya" /> According to the [[Qel-Droma Epics]], Kun was a former [[Jedi]] who turned to the [[dark side of the Force]] and became a [[Sith Lord]],<ref name="G&G" /> leading a [[Sith Empire (Exar Kun)|Sith Empire]] with fellow fallen Jedi [[Ulic Qel-Droma]]<ref name="Nexus of Power" /> around [[4,000 BBY|4000 BBY]].<ref name="Exar Kun date" /> According to the Qel-Droma Epics, the [[double-bladed lightsaber]] design dated back to [[Exar Kun's lightsaber|Exar Kun]].<ref name="G&G" />

During the [[Imperial Era]], [[crime lord]] [[Dryden Vos]] owned a [[Dryden's desk|desk]] with an [[obsidian]] slab as its base, which he had plundered from a [[Unidentified Sith temple|Sith temple]]. The [[stone]] was carved with the warding spells,<ref name="Solo Guide">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]''</ref> as well as an [[Domabesh|inscription]] reading "Our temple honouring Sith Lord Exar Kun."<ref name="Solo Guide" /><ref name="Solo">''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref>
{{Char-stub}}

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|The central desk, which represents the administrative seat of his power, is a bespoke piece of furniture. The stone base, that Dryden has plundered from the Sith temple of Exar Kun, is made from polished obsidian and decorated with carved hieroglyphs representing spells that protected its former home.|[[Lee Sandales]]|<ref name="SoloArt">''[[The Art of Solo: A Star Wars Story]]''</ref>}}
[[File:ExarKun-SWGTCGGH.png|thumb|right|250px|Exar Kun in the ''Star Wars'' Legends continuity]]
Exar Kun was first mentioned in the current ''[[Star Wars]]'' [[canon]] in ''[[Nexus of Power]]'', a [[2016]] supplement to the ''Star Wars'' roleplaying products made by [[Fantasy Flight Games]].<ref name="Nexus of Power" /> The character was created by [[Kevin J. Anderson]] and originated in the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity, where he was first mentioned, albeit unnamed, in the [[1994]] novel ''[[Jedi Search]]''<ref name="JS">''[[Jedi Search]]''</ref> before being fully introduced in the sequel released that same year, [[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']].<ref name="DA">[[Dark Apprentice (novel)|''Dark Apprentice'']]</ref> When creating the character, Anderson was initially unsure whether Kun should be a [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] or a "[[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]],"<ref name="lucasfilm22">[[The Lucasfilm Fan Club Magazine 22|''The Lucasfilm Fan Club Magazine'' 22]]</ref> finally making his decision when [[George Lucas]] voted on the former.<ref name="comicscan">{{GalaxyCite|8|ComicScan|ComicScan: Taken by Force}}</ref>

In the [[2018]] reference book ''[[The Art of Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'', ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story]]'' set decorator [[Lee Sandales]] described the [[obsidian]] stone used as the base for [[crime lord]] [[Dryden Vos]]'s [[Dryden's desk|desk]] aboard the ''[[First Light]]'' as having been plundered by Vos from the [[Unidentified Sith temple|Sith temple]] of Exar Kun.<ref name="SoloArt" /> Half of the inscription on the base can be seen in the film,<ref name="Solo" /> while the rest can be seen in the reference book ''[[Solo: A Star Wars Story The Official Guide]]''.<ref name="Solo Guide" /><ref name="Reddit">{{Reddit|url=r/aurebesh/comments/kf66n5/on_translating_the_runes_on_dryden_voss_desk|thread=On translating the runes on Dryden Vos's desk|date=2020-12-17|author=u/Ender_HappyLeviathan|archivedate=20220617040134}}</ref>

The [[2016]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]'' contains an illustration of a building resembling<ref name="Galactic Atlas">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas]]''</ref> the depiction of the [[Temple of Exar Kun]] from the [[2003]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies]]''.<ref name="SWG">{{SWGcite|exp=AED|type=poi|The Temple of Exar Kun|Yavin 4}}</ref> The [[2021]] reference book "[[Scarif and Other Planets in the Outer Rim]]," a part of [[De Agostini]]'s [[Star Wars Encyclopedia (series)|''Star Wars Encyclopedia'']] series<ref name="Scarif">{{EncyclopediaCite|Scarif and Other Planets in the Outer Rim}}</ref> contains the [[Ralph McQuarrie]] depiction of the temple from the [[1995]] reference book ''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''.<ref name="TISWU">''[[The Illustrated Star Wars Universe]]''</ref> Both depictions feature<ref name="Galactic Atlas" /><ref name="Scarif" /> a statue of Exar Kun,<ref name="DA" /> however, no connection has been made between them.
